10.1002_adfm.79490: Suppressing polysulfid shuttling and enhancing Li + desolvation kinetics are crucial for high‐performance lithium–sulfur (Li─S) batteries. Herein, we propose an elaborate molecular trap design strategy based on functional‐group decoupling and synergistic enhancement in covalent organic frameworks (COFs) to resolve the aforementioned issues. A cyano‐containing COF (CN‐COF) and its amidoxime derivative (COF‐AO) serve as cooperative dual‐sided separator coatings. CN‐COF contributes a well‐ordered porous structure for confining sulfur species; its C≡N sites interact with polysulfides to reduce the reaction energy barrier of sulfur conversion. On the anode side, ─NH 2 /─OH groups in COF‐AO promote Li + desolvation and modulate Li + transport by capturing solvent molecules via hydrogen bonding, which suppresses parasitic reactions and ensures rapid Li + migration. Besides, the regular topological structure and size‐exclusion effect of COF restrict migration of large‐sized solvent molecules and polysulfides, enabling homogeneous Li + flux and smooth Li deposition. Benefiting from these advantages, Li||Li symmetrical cells achieve stable cycling for 7000 h at 5 mA cm −2 /5 mAh cm −2 . The Li─S battery delivers an initial capacity of 820 mAh g −1 with an ultralow decay rate of 0.024% per cycle over 900 cycles at 5 C.The pouch cell exhibits a high initial capacity of 1020 mAh g −1 at 0.2 C and stable operation for 150 cycles.
10.1002_anie.2311940: The sluggish kinetics of alkaline oxygen evolution reaction (OER), together with the highly polarizing conditions at industrial‐level ampere‐scale current densities, which cause catalyst instability, motivate the search for new approaches to break the challenging activity‐stability trade‐off. Herein, we demonstrate that atomic carbon doping into the octahedral voids of Fe 2 O 3 ultrathin nanosheets (C‐Fe 2 O 3 UNSs) with constructed Fe oh III– O–Fe oh III synergistic centers can modify the coverage of * OH intermediates and allow direct * O– * O radical coupling. This enables both structural and catalytic stabilization, as confirmed by operando spectroscopic measurements and density‐functional theory calculations, with an overpotential of 227 mV to achieve 500 mA cm −2 along with 4500‐h durability. When applying C‐Fe 2 O 3 UNSs in an anion exchange membrane water electrolyzer, it delivers a cell voltage of 1.72 V at 1.5 A cm −2 while operating for 2800 h from 1 to 5 A cm −2 , with a degradation rate of 3.05 mV kh −1 at 3 A cm −2 .
10.1002_cssc.202501692: Concerted electroreduction of carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) and nitrate (NO 3 − ) to produce urea is a “three‐win” path that simultaneously achieves the high‐value utilization of CO 2 , nitrogen removal from wastewater, and green nitrogen fertilizer production. It is becoming a new frontier in artificial carbon cycling and sustainable agriculture, while there are bottlenecks in catalyst stability, catalytic performance, and mechanism insights. As a result, the large‐scale implementation of this technology still faces significant challenges. By integrating the analysis of reaction mechanisms, the design of catalytic microstructure, and the optimization of external conditions, a multiscale correlation framework among the three is established in this concept , providing a key path to bridge the acknowledged gap between molecular‐scale mechanisms and macroscopic system optimization. The objective is to expedite the industrial application of this technique and promote the utilization of waste carbon and nitrogen sources in a circular manner.
10.1016_j.microc.2026.119189: The study presents a novel electrochemical biosensor for the determination of relative antioxidant capacity using a superoxide dismutase (SOD)-based biosensor. The biosensor contains ZnO nanostructures electrodeposited onto gold-coated electrospun polycaprolactone (PCL/Au) fibers. ZnO nanostructures with different morphologies were obtained by varying electrodeposition parameters and the resulting PCL/Au/ZnO platforms were morphologically and electrochemically characterized. SOD was immobilized onto PCL/Au/ZnO through three different strategies: covalent attachment via carbodiimide chemistry, entrapment within chitosan, and physical adsorption. The performance of PCL/Au/ZnO/SOD biosensors was evaluated by cyclic voltammetry and fixed-potential amperometry to assess the influence of ZnO morphology and immobilization strategy on biosensor's analytical performance. The optimized ZnO nanostructure significantly enhanced electron transfer and enzyme immobilization, resulting in improved sensitivity, reproducibility and analytical performance compared with the other electrodeposition conditions and was successfully applied to the determination of antioxidant capacity in complex beverage matrices, including red wine, green tea, and orange juice. Unlike conventional antioxidant assays based on synthetic radicals, the proposed biosensor selectively evaluates superoxide scavenging activity, providing biologically relevant information on antioxidant capacity.
10.1021_acs.est.6c03827: Dissolved organic matter (DOM), ubiquitously present in aquatic systems, exerts a significant impact on advanced oxidation processes (AOPs), typically acting as an inhibitor. However, our investigation in this work reveals that DOM can function as an activator of molecular oxygen (O2) for selective singlet oxygen (1O2) production through an innovative electrochemical regulation strategy. A positive electric field was utilized to trigger the electrochemical oxidation of MnII in MnO, generating high-spin MnIII that targets the transformation of ortho-hydroquinone moieties in DOM to ortho-semiquinone radical (ortho-SQ•-). The metal-ligand cooperation stabilized ortho-SQ•- on the MnO surface as MnII-ortho-SQ•- complexes, which effectively activated dissolved O2 into 1O2 with •O2- as an intermediate. Elementary electron-transfer steps among high-spin MnIII, ortho-hydroquinone, and O2 were systematically elucidated, based on which a quantitative relationship between the structural characteristics of ortho-hydroquinone and 1O2 production was established. Electron-donating groups on ortho-hydroquinone showed an enhancing effect on 1O2 production by promoting the formation of surface MnII-ortho-SQ•- complexes as well as their reactions with O2. By integrating the DOM-mediated O2 activation pathway into an electrochemical oxidation system, we achieved a remarkable improvement in phenol degradation efficiency, with a twofold acceleration of the degradation rate and over 50% reduction in energy consumption. This work establishes a mechanistic framework describing how DOM synergizes with electrochemical oxidation reactions to in situ activate dissolved O2 under an electric field drive, paving a new avenue for developing innovative water remediation processes by exploiting DOM-O2 interactions in aquatic systems.
10.1021_jacs.6c11457: Developing all-solid-state batteries (ASSBs) based on high-capacity cathodes (e.g., Ni-rich and Li-rich layered oxides) offers a promising route toward next-generation batteries with high energy density and safety. However, under high voltage, the cathode/solid electrolyte (SE) interface suffers from severe chemical degradation due to enhanced cathode-catholyte interactions. Here, we propose a chemical-delithiation-induced surface reconstruction strategy for Li-rich layered oxide cathodes, as a proof of concept, to effectively eliminate cathode-catholyte interfacial chemical degradation in ASSBs. We found that chemical-delithiation treatment by NO2BF4 induces a surface reconstruction of Li-rich layered oxide, forming a cation-disordered subsurface layer, which can then incorporate fluorine alike disordered rock-salt cathodes. Such surface reconstruction passivates the oxidative surface of Li-rich cathode in which oxygen redox is prevalent at high potential, thus eliminating the interfacial chemical degradation during cycling. As a result, the treated Li-rich layered cathode achieved a reversible capacity of ∼300.3 mA h g-1 that is comparable to liquid cells and a capacity retention of 82.3% over 1500 cycles at 1 C. By extending this strategy to Ni-rich layered oxides, we further demonstrate its universality in interfacial chemical design for high-energy-density ASSBs.
